2027-04-18.title: Fourth Sunday of Easter (Good Shepherd Sunday)
readings: There is salvation in no one else; there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved
The stone rejected by the builders has become the cornerstone (or: Alleluia)
See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; we will see him as he is
The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep
2027-04-18.alt: Year B. Good Shepherd Sunday: every year the Gospel of the Fourth Sunday of Easter is taken from John 10 (Year A 10:1–10; Year B 10:11–18; Year C 10:27–30). The Church keeps the World Day of Prayer for Vocations, first kept in 1964 at the wish of St Paul VI; the Holy Father usually publishes a message for the day. The Gloria and the Creed are said; the Regina Caeli is prayed in place of the Angelus. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-18.verse: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
theo: Every year, halfway between Easter and Pentecost, the Church sets before us the face of the risen Christ as the Good Shepherd. The first reading shows us one of his under-shepherds at work. Peter and John have been arrested for healing a man lame from birth at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple and for preaching the resurrection. The next morning they stand before the rulers, the elders and the scribes, the high priestly family among them. And Peter, “filled with the Holy Spirit,” speaks. Only a few weeks earlier, in the courtyard of the high priest, this same man had been frightened by a servant girl into denying that he knew Jesus. Now he says to the most powerful men in Jerusalem: if you are asking how this man was healed, “let it be known to all of you… that this man is standing before you in good health by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead.” Then he quotes the psalm we sing today: “This Jesus is ‘the stone that was rejected by you, the builders; it has become the cornerstone.’” And he ends with one of the boldest sentences in the New Testament: “There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.” The Church has never softened this. Jesus Christ is the one Saviour of all (Catechism 432; 846). At the same time she teaches that those who, through no fault of their own, do not know him, but seek God with a sincere heart and try to do his will, can be saved by his grace, which reaches them in ways known to God (Catechism 847; Lumen Gentium 16). Peter's words are spoken to the particular leaders before him at that moment, not to the Jewish people as a whole (Catechism 597); he himself is a son of Israel announcing Israel's Messiah.

The Gospel is the heart of the day. “I am the good shepherd.” The Greek word for “good” here, kalos, also means noble and beautiful: Jesus is the true shepherd, the shepherd as a shepherd should be. Israel knew the image well. God was the shepherd of his people (Psalm 23; Psalm 80:1), and through Ezekiel he had condemned the shepherds who fed themselves instead of the flock and promised: “I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out” (Ezekiel 34:11). When Jesus says “I am the good shepherd,” he claims to be that promised shepherd, God himself come to seek his sheep. He sets himself against the hired hand, who works for wages, “sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and runs away.” The difference is not skill but love: the hired hand “does not care for the sheep.” The Good Shepherd knows his own, and they know him, “just as the Father knows me and I know the Father.” This is not a list of names on a register; it is the intimacy of the Trinity offered to each of us. Five times in these few verses Jesus speaks of laying down his life. He does it freely: “No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it up again.” In the Easter season we hear both halves of that sentence: the Cross and the Resurrection are one act of the Shepherd's love (Catechism 609). And his love is wider than any fold: “I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold. I must bring them also… So there will be one flock, one shepherd.” Today we pray for all who do not yet know him, and for the unity of all Christians in his one flock.

The second reading tells us what the Shepherd's sacrifice has made of us: “See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are.” Not only called, but made so, in Baptism. And there is more to come: “what we will be has not yet been revealed. What we do know is this: when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him as he is.” That vision of God face to face is the goal of every Christian life (Catechism 1023). This is why the Church prays today for vocations. The Good Shepherd continues to lead his flock through shepherds he calls: priests who stand in his person at the altar and in the confessional, deacons, men and women in consecrated life, missionaries, and also fathers and mothers who are the first shepherds of the domestic church. God promised through Jeremiah: “I will give you shepherds after my own heart” (Jeremiah 3:15). Kerala has received this gift abundantly, and many of her sons and daughters serve the Church across India and the world. Today let each family ask whether God may be calling one of its own, and let each of us pray for our priests by name. May the Mother of the Good Shepherd, the Blessed Virgin Mary, who gave her whole life to God's call, intercede for all who are called.
conn: On the Fourth Sunday of Easter the Gospel is always from John 10: in Year A the sheepfold and the gate (10:1–10), in Year B the shepherd who lays down his life (10:11–18), in Year C “my sheep hear my voice” (10:27–30).
World Day of Prayer for Vocations.
First kept in 1964 at the wish of St Paul VI; it is kept on this Sunday. The Holy Father usually writes a message for it each year.
The Greek word means good, noble and beautiful. Jesus is the model shepherd, the shepherd as God intended.
A worker paid by the day, with no stake in the flock. Ezekiel 34 and Zechariah 11:17 condemn shepherds who abandon or exploit the sheep.
Psalm 118:22, the great Easter psalm. Jesus applies it to himself (Mark 12:10–11), and so do Peter here and in 1 Peter 2:7.
The Sanhedrin, the supreme Jewish council in Jerusalem, presided over by the high priest; Acts 4:6 names Annas, Caiaphas, John and Alexander.
The Gentiles who would be brought into the one flock. John 11:52 says Jesus would die “to gather into one the dispersed children of God.”
The Good Shepherd in early art.
A young shepherd carrying a lamb on his shoulders is one of the earliest images of Christ, painted in the Roman catacombs in the third century.
altar: The Good Shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. At every Mass that one sacrifice of the Cross is made present, and the risen Shepherd feeds his flock with his own Body and Blood.
The priest at the altar acts in the person of Christ the Head and Shepherd. Pray for him today, and for all whom God is calling to stand there after him.
outline: Ask: who has been a good shepherd in my life?
Not a hired hand: one who knows and lays down his life.
We will see him as he is.
Point 5 · Shepherds after his own heart
“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
live: As a family, pray each evening this week for one more priest or sister from your parish, and for the seminarians of your diocese by name.
Write a short note, send a message or simply say thank you to your parish priest today.
Give ten silent minutes this week to ask the Good Shepherd: what is my vocation, and how can I live it better?
Parents: lay down a little of your life this week for your children: one evening without the phone, given entirely to them.
fathers: The Lord laid down his life for his sheep and turned his body and blood into our sacrament, so that he might feed with his flesh the sheep he had redeemed. Those of us who are shepherds must at least give our goods to the sheep; if we will not give our possessions, how shall we ever give our lives?

All good shepherds are in the one Shepherd; they are his members. Peter is a shepherd, Paul is a shepherd, but in them it is Christ who feeds the flock, for the voice of the Shepherd is heard in all of them.
Nothing so marks the shepherd as care for the flock. The one who loves Christ will feed his sheep, and the proof of love is the willingness to suffer for them.
magis: The Church is a sheepfold whose one and necessary gate is Christ, and a flock of which God himself foretold that he would be the shepherd.
Jesus freely lays down his life: “No one takes it from me” (John 10:18).
There is no other name by which we must be saved; and how God's grace may reach those who without fault do not know Christ.
Those who die in God's grace will see him “as he is” (1 John 3:2), face to face.
Pastores Dabo Vobis 1 (St John Paul II, 1992)
“I will give you shepherds after my own heart” (Jeremiah 3:15): the promise God keeps in every age through the gift of priests.
saints: Pope from 649 to 655. He condemned the error that Christ has only one will, was arrested by order of the emperor, exiled to the Crimea and died there of hardship; venerated as a martyr.
Monk, abbot of Bec in Normandy and Archbishop of Canterbury (1033–1109), Doctor of the Church, who described theology as “faith seeking understanding.”
Martyr of the early fourth century whose tomb tradition places at Lydda, the town where Peter healed Aeneas (Acts 9:32–35). Much loved in Kerala, where many churches bear his name.
2027-04-18.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, lead us to a share in the joys of heaven, so that the humble flock may reach where the brave Shepherd has gone before. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you laid down your life for us and took it up again. Call many of our young people to follow you as priests and consecrated persons, keep our pastors faithful and joyful, and gather all your sheep into one flock under you, the one Shepherd. Amen. Alleluia.

quick: Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, told the council: there is salvation in no other name than Jesus.
Jesus is the good shepherd who knows his sheep and freely lays down his life for them and takes it up again.
We are God's children now, and we will see him as he is. Today we pray for vocations.
2027-04-18.action: Pray every day this week for vocations from your own parish, and thank your priest.
2027-04-18.question: Do I listen for the Good Shepherd's voice, and what is he calling me to?
catechism: Christ the gate and the Shepherd of the flock.
He lays down his life freely.
We shall see him as he is.
kidsaint: A parish priest in a small village in France called Ars, about two hundred years ago. He was not very good at studies, but he loved Jesus and his people very much. He prayed for them, visited them, and sat for many hours every day in the confessional so that they could receive God's forgiveness. People came from all over France to see him. Lesson: a good shepherd gives his time and his heart to his sheep.
2027-04-18.special: Fourth Sunday of Easter (Good Shepherd Sunday). World Day of Prayer for Vocations. Gloria and Creed.
term: From the Latin vocare, “to call.” God's call to every person: first to holiness through Baptism, and then to a particular way of life, as a priest or deacon, in consecrated life, or as a married or single layperson. On Good Shepherd Sunday the Church prays especially for vocations to the priesthood and consecrated life.

family.explain: Jesus said: I am the good shepherd. A shepherd takes care of his sheep. He knows each one by name, he finds food and water for them, and if a wolf comes, he does not run away. Jesus loves us so much that he gave his life for us on the cross, and then he rose again. He knows each of us by name!
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest, and for boys and girls whom Jesus may be calling to be priests and sisters.
family.ask: Ask: “What could Jesus be calling me to do with my life? Let us pray about it together.”

illus: In a parish in Wayanad, a young man told his father he was thinking of the seminary. His father, a planter whose only son he was, refused even to discuss it. That monsoon the father fell seriously ill one night. It was the old parish priest, already over seventy, who came at two in the morning on his motorbike through the rain, sat with him in the hospital until dawn, and gave him the sacraments. When the father recovered, he called his son and said: if you want to be a priest, go. But be a priest like that one.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you know us and we know you. Lead us, feed us, and call many to follow you. Alleluia. Amen.
share: There is no other name under heaven… by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). Do I speak the name of Jesus with Peter's courage?
See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God (1 John 3:1). How does it change my day to know that I am God's child?
The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). For whom am I called to lay down my life, a little each day?
pm.resp: The stone rejected by the builders has become the cornerstone. Alleluia.
interc: For Pope, bishops, priests and deacons, that they may be shepherds after the heart of Christ.
For an increase of vocations to the priesthood and consecrated life, especially from our own parish and families.
For seminarians, novices and their formators.
For all who do not yet know the Good Shepherd, and for the unity of Christians in one flock.
For parents, the first shepherds of their children.
pm.close: Father, through your Son, the Good Shepherd, you lead your flock to life. Give us shepherds after his own heart, and bring us all to see you as you are. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Good Shepherd Sunday. In the middle of the Easter season the Church shows us the risen Jesus as the shepherd who knows us by name and leads us home. And today we pray in a special way for vocations.

In the first reading Peter stands before the most powerful council in Jerusalem. Only weeks before, he had denied Jesus to a servant girl. Now, filled with the Holy Spirit, he says: there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). The Good Shepherd has made a frightened sheep into a fearless shepherd.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). He compares himself with the hired hand who runs away when the wolf comes. Why does the hired hand run? Because he does not care for the sheep. The good shepherd stays, because he loves. And Jesus did not only risk his life; he gave it on the cross, freely, and took it up again on Easter morning.

He also says: I know my own and my own know me (John 10:14). You are not a number to him. He knows your name, your story, your wounds. And he has other sheep too, not yet in the fold. He wants one flock and one shepherd. So we pray today for those far from him and for the unity of all Christians.

St John tells us what that love has made of us: see what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are (1 John 3:1). One day we will see him as he is. That is where the Shepherd is leading us.

And the Shepherd still calls shepherds. Let us pray for our priests, who give their lives for us. Let us thank them. And let every family ask: could Jesus be calling one of ours? Do not be afraid if he is. There is no greater joy than to follow the Good Shepherd wherever he leads. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: I am the good shepherd. A good shepherd knows all his sheep by name. Jesus knows your name too! He loves you so much that he gave his life for you, and he rose again to be with you always.
Jesus also needs helpers to be shepherds for his people: priests and sisters. Maybe one day he will call you! Let us pray: Jesus, Good Shepherd, help me to listen to your voice.

intro: Theme: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
The one saving name, the children of God, the Shepherd who lays down his life and takes it up again, and shepherds after his own heart.

q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone. This is the LORD's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
points.apply: Speak the name of Jesus to one person this week, simply and with joy, as the reason for your hope.

sub: We will see him as he is.
q: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are. The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him.
points.apply: Begin each day this week by saying: Father, I am your child; let me live as your child today.

sub: I lay it down and take it up again.
q: For thus says the Lord GOD: I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Lay down a little of your life for someone in your care this week: your time, your comfort, your own way.

sub: Pray the Lord of the harvest.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.”
points.apply: Pray as a family every day this week for vocations, and encourage one young person who may be called.

concl: Jesus, the rejected stone and the one saving name, is the Good Shepherd who laid down his life and took it up again.
He makes us children of God, leads us to see him as he is, and still calls shepherds after his own heart.
2027-04-18.resolve: Pray daily this week for vocations from your parish and thank your priest in person.
